title: Visual, console and phone-width checks
request: Load all 19 pages on a workspace with projects and on an empty one, and report any console or Content-Security-Policy error; compare with demo v1; at 375 px no page may scroll sideways. Fix what is found without changing the design.
spec: Every page compared with demo v1 at 1440 px; no console error on any of the 19 pages, on a workspace with projects and on an empty one; no sideways scroll at 375 px. Done when the three checks are reported page by page.
plan: Start the product on spare ports, once with projects and once empty.
Load all 19 pages headless and collect console and CSP errors.
Measure horizontal overflow on every page at 375 px.
Ask the owner before changing the top bar, since demo v1 has the same overflow.
Fix in the product only and recheck all 19 pages.

decisions.decision: The owner was asked before fixing the phone overflow.
decisions.why: Demo v1 had the same overflow and the rule was not to change the UI unless asked; the owner chose to fix it in the product only.

decisions.decision: Below 640 px the breadcrumb shrinks and ellipsizes; wider screens are unchanged and demo v1 keeps its old rule.
decisions.why: The smallest change that removes the overflow without touching the desktop design or the frozen demo.

change: A product-only CSS change: the breadcrumb may shrink and ellipsize below 640 px.

findings.defect: On a phone, long page names pushed the top bar past the edge and the page scrolled sideways.
findings.scenario: At 375 px, a name such as 'Compute & jobs' or 'Evidence library' moved the theme button 7 to 19 px outside the viewport.
findings.cause: The breadcrumb was flex 0 0 auto, so it could not shrink.
findings.fix: Below 640 px the breadcrumb shrinks and its text ellipsizes.
findings.test: Measured at 375 px on all 19 pages; later covered by make browser-test (13.2).
findings.impact: On a phone, every page with a long name scrolled sideways and put the theme button 7 to 19 px off screen, so a control could not be reached without dragging the whole page.

findings.defect: The first console sweep could not be trusted.
findings.scenario: Nineteen headless Chrome instances at once hit a 25-second alarm, so a page that timed out read as 'clean'.
findings.cause: Too many browsers at once on an 8 GB machine.
findings.fix: Rerun in small batches so each page completes, and read the errors from the logs rather than the exit status.
findings.impact: Pages that hung would have been reported as clean, so the claim 'no console error on 19 pages' would have rested partly on pages that were never loaded.
findings.open: The headless check still did not exit cleanly, so its exit status could not be used; the errors were read from its logs.

measurements.name: phone width
measurements.gate: At 375 px no page scrolls sideways.
measurements.result: Zero horizontal overflow on all 19 pages after the fix.
measurements.against_gate: The gate asks that no page scrolls sideways at 375 px: zero horizontal overflow on all 19 pages after the fix, so it passes.
limits: Measured in a headless browser through an iframe harness, because headless Chrome's own narrow widths were misleading; not on a real phone.
Only one phone width was checked; narrower screens and landscape were not.
Checked by hand at that commit; the later browser tests (make browser-test) took it over.

measurements.name: console and CSP
measurements.gate: No console or CSP error on any of the 19 pages, with projects and on an empty workspace.
measurements.result: None found on either workspace, also under the stricter CSP after the fonts change.
measurements.against_gate: The gate asks for no console or CSP error on any of the 19 pages, with projects and on an empty workspace: none was found on either, also under the stricter CSP after the fonts change, so it passes.
limits: The first sweep was not trustworthy (browsers timed out), so this result rests on the rerun in small batches.
The headless check did not exit cleanly, so errors were read from its logs rather than its exit status.
A clean console says nothing about whether each page looks like demo v1; that comparison was made by eye.

outcome: Done: no console or policy error on any page, no sideways scroll on a phone, and the look matches demo v1 apart from the agreed additions.
lessons: A check that times out must not count as a pass; size parallel browser checks to the machine.
risks: Too many headless browsers at once on a small machine time out, and a page that timed out can read as clean.
A fix for the phone overflow could change the desktop design or the frozen demo v1.
An element that cannot shrink (flex 0 0 auto) pushes controls off a narrow screen.
A Content-Security-Policy that names an outside host or allows inline code lets a page load what it should not.
